To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a multi-tracer study combined with mathematical modeling is an appropriate tool to evaluate flow and transport processes and thus to understand the attenuation of organic pollutants in a gravel bed horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetland.

the flow in the gravel bed is heterogeneous with two distinct flow zones and that a significant fraction of the flow is bypassing the wetland bed and is transported through the bottom of the gravel filter.
a multi-tracer study combined with a mathematical modeling can provide detailed information on flow and transport processes of contaminants in horizontal subsurface flow constructed wetlands.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the investigation of flow and transport in wetlands and the evaluation of flow and transport conditions in a pilot scale constructed wetland system.
the development and application of mathematical models to simulate the hydrodynamic processes in constructed wetlands.
the evaluation of the hydrological conditions and flow paths in a horizontal subsurface constructed treatment wetland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flow and transport of the contaminants is complex and the results are not easy to interpret.

the removal of the main contaminant in the investigated wetland was mainly due to sorption and biodegradation in the upper sediment layer, and that the flow pattern in the gravel bed has a significant influence on the contaminant transport and retention.
a horizontal subsurface wetland system is an efficient and sustainable solution for the treatment of contaminated water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multi-tracer test is a useful tool to evaluate the hydrological conditions in the gravel bed and to determine the retention times of the wetland.
a multi-tracer approach can be successfully applied to evaluate the hydrological flow path in a constructed wetland system.
we could successfully apply the mathematical model in the simulation of the flow and transport in the wetland system and the evaluation of the tracer results.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multi-tracer study is an important tool to understand the complex flow and transport processes and their interactions in constructed wetlands.

the use of multi-tracer tests in combination with modeling approaches is a valuable tool to investigate the hydrological flow system of constructed wetlands and to understand the removal processes of organic contaminants.
the multi-tracer experiment is a useful tool for the evaluation of hydrological processes in the wetlands.
